relationships.notes: A product can have many variants (size/color/locale); each variant has exactly one parent.
Locale-specific overrides on product-level fields.
Locale-specific overrides on attribute definitions (labels, descriptions, validation messages).
An asset can be related to many products (campaign hero shot) and a product can have many assets (image gallery).
Multi-taxonomy: a product can sit in one merchandising tree node plus one or more channel-tree nodes.
Attribute groups bound to category subtrees (electronics gets screen-size; apparel gets size + color).
Each job pushes to exactly one channel destination; a channel accumulates many jobs over time.
A job publishes a batch of products to its channel.
PIM is source of truth for content; B2C-COMM commerce_products is the storefront runtime cache. One-to-one keyed by SKU.
Inventory keeps stock against the same SKU PIM publishes; loose coupling.
CPQ pulls PIM attribute schemas to drive configurator UI.
When a PLM engineering part hits release-to-market, PIM creates a merchandising shell; one PIM product can combine multiple engineering parts (bundles).
Region-specific compliance declarations flow into PIM attributes (REACH, RoHS, Prop 65).
Supplier onboarding feeds attribute data into PIM; the product can have one primary supplier and many alternates.
PIM author / content editor of the product record.
Merchandiser who gates publish.
DAM contributor who uploaded the asset.
Brand / rights reviewer who clears the asset.
Human translator or post-edit reviewer.
Admin / merchandising-ops user who launched the publish run (where not auto-triggered).

fields.title: From Data Object
fields.description: The source / subject side of the relationship

fields.title: To Data Object
fields.description: The target / object side of the relationship

fields.title: Cardinality
fields.description: Standard ER cardinality between the two data objects

fields.title: Verb
fields.description: Parent-voice verb describing the relationship (owns, manages, places, is assigned to)

fields.title: Inverse Verb
fields.description: Reverse-direction phrasing for navigation (is owned by, reports to)

fields.title: Kind
fields.description: Structural kind of the relationship, orthogonal to cardinality: `composition` (parent owns child, cascade), `reference` (loose relationship, no cascade), `association` (peer-to-peer M:N), `inheritance` (subtype / IS-A)

fields.title: Owner Side
fields.description: The parent side of the relationship: the lifecycle owner, and the end without the foreign key. Derived from relationship_type for one_to_many (source) and many_to_one (target). Set by hand only for one_to_one.

fields.title: Persona
fields.description: The kind of person who fills this relationship to users. Empty on every other relationship.

fields.title: Required
fields.description: True when a relationship's field must be filled in once both entities exist. It never makes an entity required: whether an entity installs is is_install_optional on domain_module_data_objects (SKILL.md Rule #16). A required relationship to an absent entity carries no constraint.

entity.description: The canonical entity-relationship graph between data objects, independent of any specific solution's implementation. Captures directed relationships like User owns Asset (1:N, composition), Customer places Order (1:N, reference), Employee works on Project (M:N, association), Customer is a Person (1:1, inheritance). Carries both cardinality (Cardinality) and structural kind (Kind) so the catalog distinguishes ownership from loose reference from peer association from subtype. Self-references are allowed (User directly manages User).

computed_fields.name: data_object_relationship_label
computed_fields.description: Composed from the source data object name, the relationship verb, and the target data object name. Recomputed on every write so renames in either parent flow through.

computed_fields.name: owner_side
computed_fields.description: The parent side is the one side of the cardinality, so it is derived and cannot disagree with it. Kept as written for one_to_one and many_to_many, where cardinality does not decide it.

validation_rules.name: users_relationship_is_not_many_to_many_reference
validation_rules.message: A reference to users is one person per record. Use one one_to_many relationship from users for each kind of person, or a junction entity or an association for a genuine panel or team.
validation_rules.description: Check B7b. A row-scope rule needs a single owner, and each relationship to users holds one person.

validation_rules.name: persona_only_on_users_relationship
validation_rules.message: Only a relationship to users can name a persona.
validation_rules.description: The persona is the kind of person who fills this relationship to users.
